title: Rectify mid-cycle quota-burst attribution causing incorrect invoice lines and reconciler drift
creator: Anita Shah
description: Customers have reported invoice lines that attribute burst quota usage to the wrong billing bucket when usage crosses a mid-cycle quota refresh window. This causes the nightly Stripe -> NetSuite export reconciler to generate mismatched records and leads to downstream invoice adjustments and manual refunds. The ticket covers debugging the attribution path (metering -> quota-processor -> proration engine -> export mapper), producing a code fix, tests, and a migration to correct previously exported reconciliation mismatches.
steps_to_repro:
1) Create a customer with monthly quota with a mid-cycle quota reset configured (e.g., customer synced at 00:00 UTC on billing day).
2) Consume tokens that push the account from steady usage into a configured burst band across the reset boundary (example: usage at 23:55 UTC and again at 00:05 UTC).
3) Run the nightly export job (or simulate export locally) that takes per-hour aggregates and maps them to Stripe invoice lines and then to NetSuite allocations.
4) Observe invoice line allocations: burst usage before and after reset are merged incorrectly into prior period allocation; export includes an export_id that doesn't match the reconciler's expected proration tags.
5) Compare to raw meter logs (meter-api) and quota-processor traces to see where attribution changes bucket labels.
root_cause_summary: The reconciliation drift stems from a race between the quota refresh job (which flips the active quota window) and the in-flight aggregation commit for the last minute of the prior window. The aggregator writes hourly rollups without embedding a stable quota-window identifier; later the proration logic attempts to reassign usage to quota buckets using wall-clock boundary logic that can differ by a second due to async jobs. Additionally, the export mapper relies on the first-seen bucket label which is set by an opportunistic cache that can be stale across scheduler workers. Two mistakes: (1) no stable quota-window id persisted with aggregates; (2) export mapper prefers cached label instead of authoritative aggregated metadata at export time.
proposed_solution:
1) Persist quota_window_id on hourly and minute-level aggregates at write time so attribution cannot change after the fact.
2) Update quota-refresh job to assign new window ids atomically and emit a seqno so aggregators can detect boundary conditions.
3) Modify export mapper to query the authoritative aggregate row (with quota_window_id) during Stripe/NetSuite export rather than relying on the opportunistic cache.
4) Add reconciliation repair job: detect invoices where exported allocation disagrees with authoritative aggregates and enqueue a correction workflow that: (a) flags affected invoices, (b) generates corrected export rows, and (c) issues NetSuite adjustment entries where needed.
5) Add unit/integration tests and a load test for boundary crossing patterns.
migration_plan:
Phase 1 (non-destructive): start emitting quota_window_id on new aggregates and export mapper reads the new field when present. Deploy with feature flag disabled for backfill.
Phase 2 (read-only backfill): run a backfill that computes quota_window_id for historical aggregates over the past 90 days and stores it in a separate column. This job is idempotent and throttled to avoid DB spikes.
Phase 3 (reconciler switch): flip export mapper to require quota_window_id; run reconciliation repair for invoices in the backfilled window.
Phase 4 (cleanup): after 60 days and monitoring stable, remove legacy cache-path.
Notes: NetSuite adjustments will be batched and require finance review; coordinate with finance on a runbook and communication template.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New integration tests that simulate usage crossing the quota boundary must pass.
2) Nightly Stripe->NetSuite export no longer produces mismatched allocations for test fixtures that previously failed.
3) Production rollout behind feature flag for one tenant cohort with no new reconciler mismatches for 14 days.
4) Backfill completes for 90-day window with <0.1% DB write failures and a summary report produced.
5) Reconciliation repair job produces NetSuite adjustment drafts (and Finance signs off) for at least three sampled corrected invoices.
rollout_notes:
- Deploy persistence change and aggregator modifications to staging; run end-to-end test fixtures.
- Enable read-path in export mapper behind feature flag; route 5% of production exports for a week.
- Run backfill in weekend maintenance window; monitor DB and export latency.
- After backfill, enable reparations for a single customer cohort and coordinate finance to review generated adjustments before pushing to NetSuite.
- Expand to all customers after 14 days of healthy metrics.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Add metrics: quota_window_id_missing_count, aggregate_write_latency_boundary, export_mapper_cache_miss_rate, reconciler_correction_queue_depth.
Add alert: if reconciler_correction_queue_depth > 100 for > 30m or export_mapper_cache_miss_rate increases > 5x baseline.
Add a daily reconciliation report comparing authoritative aggregate sums vs exported allocations, with a diff > 0.5% paginated for review.
comments: 2025-02-20 Anita Shah: Created ticket after finance escalated two customers with mid-cycle burst billing mismatches. Attached sample diffs and initial hypothesis. Assigned to Miguel for triage.

2025-02-21 Miguel Torres: Reproduced locally with the provided fixture. Confirmed aggregator writes lack quota_window_id and cache path returns stale labels ~2s after quota_refresh. Started breadth check to find how many tenants have quorum of affected exports.
2025-02-22 Jamie Liu (SRE): Observed export job spikes during backfill windows; recommend throttled backfill and a per-tenant concurrency cap. Added to migration plan.

2025-02-24 Miguel Torres: Initial patch submitted: writes quota_window_id for new aggregates and includes a seqno in quota_refresh. PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1487. Unit tests added. Running integration on staging now.
2025-02-26 Finance (Priya Desai): Reviewed the repair job approach. Finance requests a dry-run mode that generates NetSuite adjustment drafts rather than pushing live entries. Added as requirement.

2025-02-28 Miguel Torres: Staging integration passed for small fixture set. Backfill dry-run completed for 7 days of history with no schema regressions. Preparing runbook for weekend backfill and finance dry-run review.
2025-02-28 QA (Oliver Grant): Please add test that simulates clock skew between aggregator worker and quota_refresh service to ensure stable boundary assignment.
